answer:
Your records don't list any allergies. There's no recorded allergy to any medicine, food, or anything else.

That's good news, but it's not proof that you have no allergies. An empty list can mean two things. One is that someone asked and you said "none". The other is that nobody ever wrote one down. Your records don't say which. They also only cover what Cascade North Demo Hospital sent over, so an allergy noted by another doctor or pharmacy wouldn't show up here.

One small reassuring detail: in July 2025 you had a CT scan of your chest with contrast dye, and nothing in your records mentions a reaction to it.

If you know you react to anything, even something mild like a rash from an antibiotic, tell your doctor so it gets added. That way it's on file for future prescriptions and scans.
